records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:104: concatenatedRSToASN1DER does not validate that signature.length equals signLength, silently truncating oversized signatures and discarding appended bytes before verification. Reject incorrect lengths before copying.
records.rationale: Looking at the concatenatedRSToASN1DER method in AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java lines 104-120, the code calculates `int len = signLength / 2` and then copies from the signature array using `System.arraycopy(signature, 0, r, 1, len)` and `System.arraycopy(signature, len, s, 1, len)`. There is no validation that `signature.length == signLength`. If signature.length > signLength, the method will only process the first signLength bytes, silently ignoring any trailing bytes. records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.java:57: readSequence allows elements to extend past the declared sequence boundary. Bound element reads to the sequence’s remaining bytes.
records.rationale: Looking at ASN1Decoder.readSequence() at line 57, the method reads the sequence length, then loops 'while (length > 0)' calling readNext() and subtracting the returned bytes.length from length. However, readNext() reads arbitrary elements from the stream without being constrained to the sequence's declared boundary. If an element's declared length extends beyond the sequence's remaining bytes, readNext() will happily read past the sequence boundary. records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that ECDSAAlgorithmTest uses a single KeyPairGenerator.getInstance('EC').genKeyPair() in the constructor (line 42-43) without specifying a curve, which means all three test methods (testES256, testES384, testES512) use the same default EC curve. This is a legitimate test coverage concern - the tests claim to test ES256, ES384, and ES512 algorithms but don't actually generate keys on the appropriate curves (P-256, P-384, P-521).
